evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 形義源流通解; 字形演變
evidence.text: The database analyzes 毛 as a pictograph of human hair and animal hair/fur. It describes Zhou bronze forms as hair, sometimes with a dot below the vertical stroke as decoration, and says the dot lengthens into a short horizontal stroke in some Warring States Chu forms. It also records bronze uses of 毛 as a state/family name and personal name, and a reading as 旄 for a tail ornament. The database displays eight bronze examples and eleven Chu manuscript examples; these are source-reported forms, not a visual examination in this research.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.field: 字源字形; 金文例證
evidence.text: The character page lists bronze examples including 毛公旅方鼎 and early Western Zhou vessels, a late Western Zhou 毛鬲, Chu manuscripts, Qin slips, clerical examples, and the Shuowen small-seal form. These catalogue labels document a graphic record extending from Western Zhou bronze through later scripts, but the page does not establish the first occurrence of the hair word.
evidence.title: 毛 máo - 漢典

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.field: 《說文》; 中古音; 形義通解
evidence.text: Quotes Shuowen: 毛 refers to eyebrows/hair and animal hair, calls it 象形 (pictographic), and gives 莫袍切. Its Guangyun table records 莫袍切 with level tone and 莫報切 with departing tone. This is a historical lexicographic account, not independent proof of the depicted referent or of the earliest meaning.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.text: The page presents several graphic forms and says the forms were created from concrete images; it reports an interpretation of 毛 as depicting hair branching, while explicitly presenting that as one scholarly view. I could not establish from the accessible text whether this interpretation is the page's own preferred analysis or inspect its glyph images, so it does not settle whether the graph depicts a feather, hair, or another hairy form.
evidence.title: 毛字形演变字源

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.text: The database says毛 was used in bronze inscriptions as the name of a state and lineage, and as a personal name. It gives 班簋 as an example of a 毛伯 title and 召伯毛鬲 as a personal name. These are graph uses for proper names; without further evidence they do not establish that 毛 was borrowed as a spelling for an unrelated spoken word.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.text: The database reports a bronze use of 毛 read as 旄, denoting a tail ornament on a standard, and gives 嫊奚鼎's 毛兩 as an example. This is a reported phonetic-loan use of the whole graph; it does not make 毛 a phonetic component in its own structure. The underlying source word and independent evidence for its pronunciation are not supplied here.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫 (CUHK Multi-function Chinese Character Database)
evidence.text: The database explains the adjective sense ‘fine/small’ as an extension from the small, fragmentary nature of hairs. This is a proposed semantic path, not a dated sequence of attestations; the page does not show when this extension first appeared.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.field: 說文解字; 音韻方言; 字源字形
evidence.text: The page quotes the Shuowen definition 眉髮之屬及獸毛也 and its pictographic analysis; gives modern Mandarin IPA mɑu˧˥ and Tang-period *mɑu; and lists Japanese MOU/BOU (on), KE (kun), Korean MO, Vietnamese mao, and Cantonese mou4. It also catalogues bronze, Chu manuscript, Qin slip, clerical, and seal-script forms. The page’s character-specific presentation supports that these are readings of 毛, not an ancient pronunciation of a pictured object.
evidence.title: 毛 máo - 漢典

evidence.source: Local Baxter–Sagart dataset; upstream transcription checked against Wiktionary Chinese 毛 page
evidence.text: Local row for 毛 records Mandarin máo, Middle Chinese maw, Old Chinese *C.mˤaw, gloss ‘hair’, and GSR 1137a. Wiktionary's character page lists Zhengzhang Shangfang (2003) 毛 *maːw, *maːws separately. These are different reconstruction systems and should not be merged. The local dataset contains no phonetic component to compare because 毛 is treated here as a pictograph.
evidence.kind: local structured reading cross-check with external character page
evidence.title: 毛 - 维基词典，自由的多语言词典

gaps: No securely dated earliest attestation of 毛 meaning hair, fur, or feather was established. Bronze examples are documented, but database snippets classify some as names and a proposed 毛-for-旄 reading; they do not date the common noun sense.

The accessible paleographic resources' image glyphs were not visually inspected. The Academia Sinica evolution page exposes period labels but not textual shape descriptions for 毛. Therefore the exact shape sequence, first attested form, and any graphic corruption remain uncertain.

The graph's original depicted referent is not settled by the inspected text: sources call it hair/human and animal hair, while the dossier says feather; one secondary page reports a scholarly branching-hair interpretation. No independent basis here identifies an original feather species or depicted object.
Shuowen's pictographic explanation is recorded as a Han-period lexicographic analysis, not treated as direct confirmation of the Shang/Zhou graph's original referent.

A semantic extension from hair's fine/frangible nature to ‘small/fine’ is asserted by CUHK, but no dated bridge or earliest attestation was found. Other senses such as coarse, unprocessed, or barren were not ordered chronologically.

CUHK reports whole-graph 毛 used for 旄 in a bronze inscription, but the underlying word's earliest independent attestations and the historical pronunciation of the ornament's name were not independently established. This remains distinct from any claim about 毛 as a phonetic component.

The dossier's Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparison is not independently established by primary lexical sources in this search. Cognacy with 眉 and Tibeto-Burman comparanda remains a comparative-linguistic proposal, not a fact inferred from graphic form.

The local Baxter–Sagart row for 毛 is *C.mˤaw; this is consistent with the dossier. There is no proposed sound component in 毛 itself to compare. Zhengzhang readings on Wiktionary are a separate system and include *maːws; they were not reconciled across systems.
The local HSK 1 kMandarin row gives máo. Official Unicode Unihan character record access failed, so the requested official click-through citation remains unavailable.
The first search audit URLs include some result pages that were not opened or were inaccessible; their result snippets were not relied on as verified evidence.
